elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 4.3 opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall...", so both exit events and all causes are covered.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 4.3(a) provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period is stated. To reach preferred, change to "for a period of up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: 4.3(a) is silent on pricing; no "at HDI's then-current rates" language appears.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 4.3(b) requires HDI to "export and deliver to the Company all Content, user information and other data of the Company within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: 4.3(b) specifies no format; the words "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" are absent.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No limb (c); the insertion contains no post-return deletion obligation and no written certification of deletion.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" anchors both limbs (a) and (b) to every covered exit event.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 4.3(a): "provide the Company with transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — no request precondition limiting it to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 4.3(b) requires export and delivery of "all Content, user information and other data of the Company within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination" — the 30 days runs from the exit event, not from a request.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted 4.3 ties both limbs to "expiration or termination ... for any reason", grants at least 90 days of assistance, and requires export within 30 days after the exit event.

Preferred is not reached: no six-month assistance period, no then-current-rates charging basis, no machine-readable format specification, and no post-return deletion/written certification. These are the exact repairs needed if the preferred level is later pursued.

Minimality holds: a single concise two-limb insertion in the termination section, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or expense-allocation language, no procedural or boilerplate extras, and no deletion or paraphrase of existing 4.1 or the Termination Payment mechanic.

Intent preserved: the auto-renewal/90-day notice mechanic, the Termination Date definition and the quarterly Termination Payment schedule in (c) all survive unchanged and are not contradicted; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced. Drafter should confirm no existing subsection is already numbered 4.3 in Section 4 to avoid a duplicate reference.
Omission of a rate basis for the 90 days of assistance is customer-favourable and is not an intent or minimality defect at the fallback level; note it in the rationale only.
